# The tier 3 path list. A pull request touching any of these needs a
# line-by-line read by the repository owner before it merges.
#
# This is the single source of truth, on purpose. The list used to live in
# three places — a grep pattern in tier-gate.yml, a table in docs/WORKFLOW.md,
# and prose in CLAUDE.md — and the failure mode of that arrangement is the
# worst one available: a path added to the documents but not the pattern gives
# a gate that is written down and does not fire. Nobody notices, because the
# document says it is covered.
#
# tier-gate.yml builds its pattern from this file, and tests/test_tier3_paths.py
# fails if the documents drift from it.
#
# Entries are matched as a literal prefix against `git diff --name-only`, so a
# trailing slash covers a directory. Only `.` is escaped before the match — do
# not write regular expressions here.
#
# Adding a line is itself a tier 3 change, because .github/ is on the list.

# Authorisation and configuration. A mistake here is invisible until someone
# who should not have access has it.
src/soma/serve/oauth.py
src/soma/config.py

# Secrets, and the script that mints credentials.
.env.example
scripts/agent_token.sh

# Deployment and CI. A mistake here reaches the Pi, or disables the checks that
# would have caught the next one.
.github/
deploy/
compose.pi.yaml
Dockerfile

# The rules an agent works under. These ship no code, but changing them changes
# every future pull request.
CLAUDE.md
docs/WORKFLOW.md
